segments.translation: They came when I was working in Lyons Switch, when I was watching that old woman. Someone had cameras and microphones about that killing.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Lyons Switch.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: That killing that went on at Mulberry somewhere. They asked me about that. Ooo, I was embarrassed.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I thought it was funny. “I'm going to be on TV tonight,” she told me. I said, “What did you do?” Really, they came to that old lady's house.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, I told them she was over there, and she was.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: She was on TV and didn’t even know anything.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I didn’t know anything. I just told them we need God back in our lives. Everybody needs God in their life, that was all I said the last time.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: You said that reporter was not giving up.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: No, when I said that, they moved.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: As for me, when Mankiller was the chief, a lot were doing me like that. Take pictures of me talking. That is what she told me herself, “Wilma, call me in.” She said, “They are going to talk to you. It is going to be about this, so just know. So, they called and did like it is here. And so they said, “We are going to talk about this.” I said OK. They told me, “When I do this, start talking.” I was sitting there and when they did this [gesture], I didn’t know what to say. I forgot everything.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: The same would happen to me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They were still doing this at me [gesture].

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: You could have said I just did it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do y'all remember that one common value, common ground? That was me. That was what I did, and the thing was on fire. What was it? I don’t remember. There was a lot. Sometimes I would be in a store, and someone would hear me talking. They would say, “You are that man, you are that man.”

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: “You want my autograph?”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That is what they would say. They would recognize hearing me talking and say, “You are the one who says that.”

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I think it is good what they have on TV at the Cherokee clinic, talking about something, you know, making a video. I was sitting there and Lawrence Scott came on, and I thought, “Huh!” It was almost Halloween, and he started talking about ghosts, I thought that was funny.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about that belief that we have? Have you ever seen a ghost?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I really have.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Tell me a little about it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: There were a lot of them long time ago. There really were ghosts living once. Do you remember where Luther Worley had that bus parked and sold beer?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: My uncle and his friend George Duck said, “Let's go buy two quarts.” I told them I'm going, so we were coming across the field at Cherry Tree where the road is at Duck Lane. We went that way toward the field. There is a cemetery there where there were lots of houses and some trees, there was cemetery there. We were walking right there, and a flame was this big out [gesture]. It was about this tall [gesture], and it had a tail this long [gesture]. It wasn’t fast. It was going slow, and it came close from this way. And my uncle and him said, “Look, ghosts!” And it scared me, too. They said, “Gah-lee!” So it stopped for a little while by where we were standing, and it landed over there in that cemetery. They forgot about the beer.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They went home.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They took off running with me right behind them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It was following y'all.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And then, that Bill Auffets orchard...

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Used to be a creek. There was a house near there. My aunt was over there. They were drinking there, and me and my uncle were outside. My uncle said, “I wish they would hurry up.” We were waiting on my aunt. She and her husband was in there. One just like that came, it went by real slow, and it went and landed behind the house. My uncle hollered and told my aunt, “Let's leave right now! A ghost came!” So my aunt believed it, and when we came back, she left her husband.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Your aunt didn’t see it? The fire.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, she just believed it. My uncle was scared when he was telling her. It really came just right there. Man, it scared me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did it just fade away or what?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yes, it just faded away right there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do they not call them kolen, Charlie?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yes, I have heard them called that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes, kolen ani kolen they call them (raven mockers).

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, I have heard of that.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: One time when Joe Scott lived in front of Cherry Tree store, the one that draws, I was over there one time, and I said, “Have you ever seen one?” I told him that I had seen that. He said, “You ain't going to believe this, but I painted what I seen.” He went and got the picture. Boy, it was big, too. It was the same thing that I seen.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That was it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: He had painted it. All the pretty colors, too, it was a beautiful flame with a tail, but it was round and red, kind of a red flame, a flame like red-orange. But it had a beautiful tail.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Long.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: It was kind of blue and that is what he painted. I said, “Gaw, we seen the same ghost!” What we seen, that is what he had drawn. He said, “That is what a booger looks like, ain't it? That is what a booger looks like,” he told me. He said, “There are a lot of people that do not know what a ghost is.” And that is what he had.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: That’s me, I never...

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You haven’t seen anything.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: No, that’s what I mean. I didn’t think of stuff like that. I was just a kid.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And we lived in town in a big white house. Me and Mom lived with my grandpa and grandma. There was a ghost that lived there. It sounded like it was breaking dishes. It sounded like it was breaking them in the kitchen. When you went in there it wasn’t nothing. It would be making a sound. It would be making noise.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Like it was mad.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And Mom would say, “Don’t be afraid. It will not do anything to you. It is just having a fit.” There wasn’t anything wrong when you went in there, but it sounded like it was breaking them. I never did see it, but I was always hearing what it was doing.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Something bothered you, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Ah, man.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was disturbing you.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I grew up with something disturbing me.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: For a long time.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Mom used to say all the time, “You should get help. I am hard-headed.” I would say, “I am not, Mom.” I told her, “Mom, if my God is for me, who can be against me? She would always say, “Someone can help you. We can go there. I said it again: “Mom, if God is for me, who can be against me?” But she was always urging me. It was doing bad.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: You said it used to get on you, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: It would choke me.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: He said it was a woman, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I would have scratches, on me when I woke up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was the same for me, that still happens to me now. One time my back was itching. I told her, “Look at my back, it was itching, really itching.” She said, “Look what it's like.” It was like someone did this, and I had been scratched.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, for me, it was three all the time, three right here [gesture].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: For me, when it began, for a long time it was on my back. Then, after a while, it was on my toes. They would be just like someone did this. And then, this last time, it was here [gesture], just two or three weeks ago. It still does that to me now.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: You know what they told me, who it was? It was one of my relatives. It probably was Skvyetsi’s daughter, because she knew a little bit about that.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Viola.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They said, “Do you know why it was doing that to you? I said, " Why is it?” They said, “It raped you.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, that is what Mama used to say, too.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I told her, “Shhhiiii, th they said it really was doing that to you.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, Mama would say the same thing.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, that is what they told me.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: That is what Mom would say, too.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I'm glad.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I told him, don’t let it do that to you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You were getting jealous.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They did exist really, because when we first moved to Cherry Tree, I was about 10 or 11. We were playing ball. I was hearing Tsilag’s two sons. They said Dad is going to be coming soon. He said we better go to the front, because he said, “I don’t want to wait on you boys.” So we were sitting in the ditch, talking. We were hearing something making a sound toward Mom’s. It was loud, too, it sounded like someone, but not a screech owl. Tsilag came there driving a flatbed. It was a standard. He shut it off and came where we were sitting real quiet. One of them said, “Dad, what is this?” Tsilag quickly said, “Boys, get in here right now. That is a ghost.” It scared us, so they left really fast. I thought, “What is he thinking?” Long time ago, flashlights were not very good. Mom had one like that. Me and that other boy went and got that, and went around back. I saw its eyes. They were red, about this big [gesture]. It had big eyes. It was a screech owl it was this big, and it was white. Mom told me they call it an owl. It was round. I kind of like it, but it was big. It had a big head. Its eyes were red. I told him, “Look at that.” I had a gun, a .22. I went and got it. I told that boy to aim that light at it. So he aimed at it and I shot nothing. It was just still standing there. I was missing it. I put it down and shot it so when I shot it, I heard it hit. It just did this [gesture]. It was standing behind that tree. It was doing this [gesture], so when I shot it, it backed up. Then it was coming doing this [gesture]. Boy, we took off running to the house. I told Mom and she said, “Why did you shoot it?” Mom got on to me. I got brave, but it wasn’t anywhere. It was probably about two nights later, I had a basketball goal. That boy was walking in front. He had the ball and was doing this [gesture]. We were walking and I did this [gesture], and looked. Gaw! It was like this watching us. Me and that boy, just right there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It was perched up there?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, it was floating in the air.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: It was you. It was telling you.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: It was floating in the air. It was like this when I saw it. I said, “Gaw!” When I said that, it did this quickly [gesture].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It faded away.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: But that was it. It was big and it was just close to where we were walking like this. That really scared me. For a long time, I didn’t hardly go out when it was dark in the back. One time it was daylight, my uncle said, “Gaw! Look at what's perched up there!” There was a big dead tree. It was right on that bluff line. There were four big ones perched up there like that. They were big, you could tell from that far. I bet it was a mile or a quarter of a mile anyway.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: You could see them good.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Up that hill, they were perched up there, four of them. Boy, my mom was always getting on to me for going up there. She was telling me there was something up there. And the little people will get you lost, too, she told me. And they will get you lost, too. That is what they did to me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They got you lost?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, it got dark on me, I would go there all the time in the back and I came out at Fog Hollow.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You went a long ways.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, it was already dark, I took off running.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Then you realized.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Then I realized, and thought, “What am I doing here?” I knew what had happened.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you not hear them talking?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, I didn’t hear them. Some say they can hear them. One time, a friend of mine was telling about how they healed him. His heart, he had heart surgery. “I was almost dead laying in bed. My wife was cooking. She came in and told me someone was going to be here, a little man, she said. And really, two came in. “Someone is going to come in.” An old person came in with long white hair. “They are going to pray for you.” So when they started praying, I started praying, too, he said. “So when they got quiet, I opened my eyes. I knew something had happened. I started immediately feeling better. I was still laying down and could not move. I quickly sat up and put my feet on the floor. I knew that God had healed me. I just got up right there, and walked to the kitchen, and scared my wife. She screamed. ‘It's OK, it's OK!’ And I told her what happened. God healed. I have been good since. Nothing bad has happened. They really did come into where I was laying.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Little people?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: One time that same man when I was a teenager. Where Claud Livers lived on Fletcher Mountain, where that creek is when it rains. There, all the time, Thomas Wofford, he was always hunting there when I was growing up. So we didn’t go that way. He just stayed over there by himself. All of us boys knew that it was his part over there. He would sit there, and one time he told me he was just sitting. “I was just sitting there, I was sitting on the bluff,” he said. He had some beagle dogs that chased deer. They were really mean, they would bite you, he said. And so they left, and he was just sitting there with them barking close - they were coming back. When he looked at the water, a lot of little people came. There really was a lot, he said. They started washing at the creek, he said. “Them dogs were coming so I better go tell them. I started hollering at them, ‘Mean dogs are coming!’ They were not hearing me. They were not listening. They were just right there. When I realized they were getting close, I thought gah-lee, this it! They are going to eat those little people. So when those little people figured out those dogs were coming, they all got in the water and were standing up straight. All the dogs were just sniffing close to them. They just got a drink of water and left. They didn’t even see them people.”

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: They couldn’t smell them once they got in that water.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They couldn’t smell them and couldn’t see them. “They suddenly went away,” he said, “the little people.” “Did that really happen?” I thought as I was sitting there. He seen something amazing - little people washing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Even if they were not washing, that is still amazing.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, it is amazing that he has seen them that much.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I really have seen something where big Roy lives at Cherry Tree. It was about that tall [gesture] but I didn’t see his face, just back. He was walking down the hallway.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It's wonder they didn’t get Tom lost.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Mom was also telling all the time.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Probably his friends, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: “If you see one, don’t tell anyone,” Mom would tell me. “Don’t tell anyone if you see one like that.” I said, “Why?” “I am telling you, don’t do it.”

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: When I saw one, I thought it was a leprechaun. That is what it looked like you know. It was just, you know, messy hair.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is that true?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It didn’t comb its hair.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: No, it had long hair.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about that Bigfoot they talk about?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: There was one living by the house.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Cherry Tree.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: There was one living in Cherry Tree when we moved there. A long time ago there were not any houses. There were two ponds there. And what they call Indian peaches. There were lots of trees there in that field. There was one tree when me and Mom moved there, behind Mom’s. A long time ago, nobody had a yard light. It would be really dark. You could not see your hand if you had it like this [gesture]. Sometimes it would be dark when the sun wasn’t shining. When that happened, man, there would be something making noise on the mountain. I knew it wasn’t a bear. I think that is what it was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you didn’t see it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, my uncle said he seen one on Sallisaw Creek.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Jimmy Ray, Jimmy Ray Sawney, Wile Atsili’s stepson.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He used to wear a hat, that one.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yes, no.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Am I thinking of a different one? So, he had seen it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what he said. Towards Sallisaw Creek. It sounded really scary.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So, y'all could hear it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, they didn’t have four-wheelers. Hardly anybody ever went to Doublehead Mountain. That is a mean mountain. It's hard to climb. You wouldn’t even be able to get off of it, except in few spots you could get down. The rest of it is a bluff. It's just all bluff. I used to go over there all the time. I never did see anybody and then when they got four-wheelers. The four-wheel-drive four-wheelers, people started...

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: And cameras.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Then people started coming up there. I was telling them, a long time ago, that was my mountain. “There ain't nobody crazy enough to go up there,” I was saying. There are rattlesnakes living up there, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: A lot of them, big ones?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They would come all the way to our house.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yeah, over there where Mom was living.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They have killed a lot of them there. One time, I had just got back around one or two. It would still be daytime when I got back. I had just got back. I just layed down on the floor by the fan. We didn’t have an air conditioner. I was laying there and that boy came in and said, “Gaw, Dad, there is a snake there.” He told me, and I was almost asleep. He was pushing me, saying, “Get a gun, Dad. It is big.”

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: He was going that way.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I said, “I will. Just get that shovel.” He pushed me hard and said, “Get a gun, Dad, it is big.” So I got a gun and started walking. He pulled me back - I almost stepped on it. I didn’t see it. It was sitting there, this big [gesture]. Coiled up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was coiled up?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: But it was so big, it was about that tall [gesture]. It was sitting there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Gaw.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: That rattle snake had a head this big. [gesture]

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: What about the one you killed at the house?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And those children, last year, last summer - last fall. They had a pool. It was pretty good-size pool. They had just come in, and I forgot something. I was going to give that dog water, and when I went out the back, I thought, “Gaw! What is that?” It was a snake this big [gesture]. It was coming like this [gesture]. I was standing there, it was coming like this [gesture]. I started looking for something to hit it with but there wasn’t nothing. It was looking, yeah, it was about this high [gesture]. It did this [gesture]. I thought, “Boy, it's going to chase me.” I started running. I knew there was a shovel way over there. I went and got it, and I started walking that way [gesture]. It was getting mad. Its head was getting flat. I thought it was a rattlesnake, but it didn’t have those things.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What do they call those?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Boy, it was the kind that is mean.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Water moccasin, is it not?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: It was one like that, I was thinking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It wasn’t a rattlesnake?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, it wasn’t. Then, when it found out, it got mad. I let it go for a while, so when it went this way, [gesture] I started running. I barely caught it with a shovel. That is how big and tough it was. I couldn’t kill it. I don’t know what it was that came to the house. I was glad the children were not outside. I took a picture of it, ain't it, and asked people what kind it was.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: What did they call it? Water moccasin, they said, ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Was its head getting flat?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: There are some that exist like that.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: It was brown.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Adder, puff adder, they call them.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: You know you can tell if they are mean by how the head is? It had a head like that. It came quickly on us at the house. I had cut the grass real good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It’s a little bit like a cobra. Was it like that? I have seen one like that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Me, one time I was cooking hog meat for that new Baptist church. They were going to have a feast. The oldest one, Keith, he was just a little boy. I just put the tailgate down on the pickup, and I just had it setting on there. He was playing around, and something happened. I put him in the truck, that boy. Then I went that way [gesture]. I did something and I was coming back. Already a rattlesnake was standing as high as the tailgate where the meat was. It was doing this [gesture]. I quickly got that boy out. I went and got a wood, and hit it with it. I wasn’t able to kill it. It got away from me. It went across the road. I was trying, I was hitting it in the head, but that wood kept breaking. It was just this long [gesture] I had it. I got scared to do anything with it. It got away from me. I wasn’t able to kill it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: Do you know where Myrtle Kirk lives?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: There are some big snakes that go through there. Woodrow Teehee said he almost got killed by one. He said he had three dogs that were looking for squirrels. Two went on and stayed near him. He said a huge snake came out. “We didn’t know,” his family said. “He never told us,” they said. Woodrow really loved me. He would really talk to me and tell me everything. He said that dog seen it and went that way. And it bit him one time and killed that dog. He said he ran and climbed a tree. He was showing me - it was a good seven or eight foot he climbed. He said that snake got there and looked at him. He said it had a head this big [gesture]. It was bigger than a stovepipe.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Big as a tree.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And the smell.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was giving off that smell.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: That smell was hard, he said. He said when he would move, it was making it mad. It was doing this [gesture]. He said he thought it was going to bite him and it was doing this [gesture]. So the two dogs came back. He said it was loud when it hit the ground. That is how heavy that snake was. It made that sound toward them dogs. He said it was fast. It would bite those dogs one time, and they would die. So when it killed those two, it went back the way it came, crawling real slow, he said. Woodrow got sick and layed in the hospital for a week, and they didn’t know what was wrong with him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was that smell it was giving off.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: That’s it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It made him sick.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: That is what made him sick. He said it almost killed him. And his relatives didn’t know. They said he never told them about it. They said, “You are the first one he has ever told.” I was surprised he didn’t tell his own kinfolks.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: They would not believe it.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And Janet Kirk was telling me there is one that comes over there, and she said it was as big as a stovepipe. It's big and it will be laying in the yard, she said. And Harold Bunche’s boy went by on a motorcycle at Dahlonegah. They were practicing ball, and he came back. I was sitting in the pickup. I always have a gun in the seat, a magnum.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: He had big eyes, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: He was scared. He said, “Boy, Kenneth, there is a giant snake on that dirt road. I thought it might knock me off my motorcycle, so I just turned around,” he said. “It's this big, Kenneth,” he was telling me. He said, “It’s a giant snake.” I said, “Let’s take off.” We went that way. He stopped there. I said, “Where was it?” He said, “It's right down there.” I was throwing rocks, trying to make it rattle or something. That boy was pulling me, saying, “Kenneth, don’t. It might jump out of them weeds and jump on you.” He said, “I bet that thing can jump a long ways. He was doing this [gesture]. “It's this big, it's this big a rattlesnake. He’s got a head that big [gesture], Kenneth. It's going to get you,” he was telling me. He was scared. He said, “I thought it was going to knock me off my motorcycle, and jump up and bite me. It was that big laying across. It was just right there when I saw it,” he said. He turned that dirt bike around. Right there, he was riding a dirt bike. That boy was scared.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I know. What are the snakes going to think now that the road is paved? It's paved now, that Dahlonegah road.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It is new now, ain't it?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: They have a new road now.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did your parents, grandmother or grandfather ever talk about if they were involved in the Trail of Tears?

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: No, I have never heard anything about how they came.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Now I am going to ask you this last thing. This Cherokee that we are speaking, what do y'all think is going to happen?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: If they don’t do anything, it is going to run out.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I think that is true, it's going to run out.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: I forget how to say things.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: We speak different.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: She is from Bell and I from Cherry Tree. It is different.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It's different. They call it dialect. It’s the same at Greasy and also Belfonte.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Why is it like that?

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: And Oak Ridge.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They talk kind of slow.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I think it's going to be good, what they are doing teaching them Cherokee. The kids are going to learn.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: If you listen to Oak Ridge, they will say that is how it really is.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: And at Bell, that is true.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They sing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We are going to finish now. I appreciate y'all coming. We really had a good conversation.

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: I had fun, too. I am grateful.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I really do thank y'all for coming.

segments.speaker: kenneth-littledeer
segments.translation: What is your name?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Dianna

segments.speaker: norma-littledeer
segments.translation: Diane Kimball, Marie and Diane.
